note: No .env file is committed and no secret values were found. The service role key is server-only. The app makes no model call from the browser, so there is no ai_browser_call. It has no LLM tool use, so there are no ai_tool_unbounded or ai_fake_tool items. AI output only writes tags, collections and a shared insight cache. docker/migrations duplicates scripts/ file for file. supabase/migrations lacks the 017-019 quota columns and the check_and_increment_ai_limit function, so a database built from that folder alone gets errors on every server-key AI call. docker/migrations has 017-019, but its README table lists only 001-016. The trending alert text says doubled in stars this month, but isTrending comes from a 7-day velocity label (components/proactive-alerts.tsx 94, app/api/github/health/route.ts 177-201). | Second labeler: scripts/ and docker/migrations/ hold identical migration copies, so migration labels cite scripts/ only. UI components were covered by targeted grep, not read line by line. No ai_browser_call found. All model calls run in Next.js API routes. The bring-your-own key goes from the browser to the app's own server in a header. RLS is on for every user table, and composite owner foreign keys block cross-user tag and collection links. Cron and test-observability routes check CRON_SECRET. README and issue markdown render through react-markdown without raw HTML. No committed secrets. Both env examples hold placeholders only.

labels.what: profiles_update_own lets a user update any column of their own profiles row, and authenticated has GRANT ALL on profiles (line 868). All AI quota state lives on profiles: ai_*_count, the week and day starts, last_ai_categorization_at, last_personalized_search_at, last_contribution_scan_at and single_repo_scan_day_count. A user can reset them with the public anon key and bypass every server-key AI limit.
The same profiles_update_own policy with no column limit. Later scripts add the AI quota columns to profiles, so users can reset their own quotas.
Duplicate of scripts/001. The same profiles_update_own policy with no column limit lets users reset their own AI quota columns.

check_and_increment_ai_limit is SECURITY DEFINER. It takes the user id and the limits from the caller and has no REVOKE or GRANT. Default privileges give EXECUTE on new functions to anon and authenticated. Anyone with the public anon key can call it by RPC with another user's id to use up that user's AI quota.
Duplicate of scripts/019. The SECURITY DEFINER quota function takes any user id and limits from the caller, with no REVOKE, so anon callers can use up another user's AI quota.

get_valid_token and token_needs_refresh are SECURITY DEFINER functions that take any user id and are granted to anon (lines 822-824, 840-842). get_valid_token returns that user's provider_token. The column is gone in this snapshot, so the call fails today, and scripts/014 drops both functions. The live-schema dump still creates them.
The browser Supabase client uses NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY. It is public by design. .env.example line 11 holds only a placeholder.

GitHub OAuth access and refresh tokens are stored in plain text in github_oauth_tokens. The repo's own hardening plan says they must be encrypted before launch. signOut in lib/auth.ts 68-74 clears the cookie but leaves the stored token row.

OAuth asks for read:user user:email public_repo read:org notifications. No code uses read:org or notifications, and public_repo grants write access to all of the user's public repos. The same string is copied in components/landing-auth-buttons.tsx 20.
Second copy of the broad OAuth scope string, with unused read:org and notifications and write-capable public_repo.
Third copy of the broad OAuth scope string, with unused read:org and notifications and write-capable public_repo.
The user's own OpenRouter, OpenAI or Anthropic API key is stored in localStorage, where any script on the origin can read it. It is sent in an x-ai-key header on AI calls.

The search query has no length limit before it is joined into three prompts (lines 381, 531, 584) with no guard. The 500-character DB check only applies when the result is cached, after the model calls. A user with their own key has no limit at all.

The whole opportunity object comes from the client body. Title and body are cut to size, but repoDescription, topics, labels, contributionTypes and risks are unbounded and go straight into the paid prompt.

Third-party issue titles go into the prompt with no guard. The model's summary and recommendation are written to the global repo_insights row that every user reads. A user with their own key can force refresh=true with no limit (route lines 37, 129-131) and overwrite that shared row.
The repo sample comes from the client. It is capped at 100 items, but each name and description is unbounded and joined into the prompt.
The prompt asks for 3-5 GitHub queries. The schema at 87-94 only has min(1), and the code runs every returned query plus one more in parallel against the GitHub API (417-425).
The prompt asks for 2-4 themes. The schema at 28-36 has no max, and each theme triggers a GitHub search.
The prompt says 1-3 collections and 1-3 tags per repo. Code filters to the known vocabulary but never caps the count. The 15-25 tag vocabulary size at line 123 is also not checked (line 143).
The prompt asks for exactly 3 evidence bullets of at most 60 characters. The schema has no count or length limit, and the bullets are shown and cached as they come.
Model output creates tags and collections and assigns them to the user's repos straight away, with no preview or approval step. The user starts the run, but the AI's choices are written directly.
categorizeRepos silently keeps only the first 500 repos, while the route accepts up to 5000. The same limit has two different values.

The route reports categorizedRepoCount as all eligible repos, not the 500 actually analyzed. The toast says Categorized N repos. Repos past 500 are never categorized, because later runs only look at repos starred after the last run (lines 192-202).

The brief limit is 20 per week and 7 per day in code, but the UI says 10/week and so does the scripts/012 comment. The intel message in components/repo-intel-tab.tsx 466 also says 10/week when the daily cap of 5 is what was hit.

Star sync stops after 50 pages (5000 stars). upsertStarredRepos then deletes every user_starred_repos row not in that list (171-192), so users with more than 5000 stars lose notes, tags and collections on older stars at each sync. An empty fetch deletes all rows (154-158).

The self-hosted cron runs @daily (midnight), while the README and vercel.json say 02:00 UTC. The job calls curl, which the node:22-alpine image does not include. CRON_SECRET in the command is likely not expanded, so star snapshots may never be recorded.
Builds ignore TypeScript errors.
tracesSampleRate is hardcoded to 1.0 on server and client, so every request is traced in production.
Model ids for each provider are hardcoded, so users and operators cannot change them without a code change.

The 200-tag and 50-collection caps are checked only in browser code, through the anon-key client called from the settings page. RLS insert policies allow unlimited rows, so a user can skip the check with direct inserts.
Unused fixture file with sample tags, collections and repos, including invented personal notes. Nothing imports it.
Landing page snapshots show hardcoded repos, star counts, statuses and contribution match scores (423-449) as product screens.
After login the redirect host comes from the x-forwarded-host header. On a host that passes this header through, a crafted request can redirect to another domain.
The Docker socket is mounted into the ofelia cron container. That container has root-level control of the host.
Star, issue and README rate limits live in an in-memory Map per process. On serverless hosting each instance counts separately, so the limits do not hold.

owner and repo from the request body go into GitHub API paths without validation or encoding, using the user's token. A value with ../ could reach other GitHub endpoints such as /user/following. The DELETE handler (lib/github.ts 184) and the issue route (app/api/github/issue/route.ts 56) do the same.
unstarRepo puts owner and repo from the request body into a DELETE GitHub API path with no validation or encoding, using the user's token.
owner, repo and number from the query string go into a GitHub API path with no validation or encoding, using the user's token.
The personalized search cooldown and the single-repo scan counter use read then write with no lock. Parallel requests can pass the check together.

The 200-tag and 50-collection per-user caps (also lines 385-391) run in browser code against the anon client. RLS allows the inserts, and no database rule enforces the caps, so a user can create unlimited rows directly
Prompt asks for 5-12 collections and 15-25 tags. TaxonomySchema has no array bounds, and lines 136-143 accept whatever count the model returns
Model output is written straight into the global repo_insights cache that every user reads for 7 days, with no review
Star button never checks response.ok, so it shows Starred even when the API returns 401, 429 or 500. The tags and collections picked in the popover are never saved (see next label)

Tag and collection assignment looks up user_starred_repos by github_repo_id, a column that table does not have. The lookup errors, the error is ignored, nothing is written, and the route still returns success
Unstar cleanup uses the same missing github_repo_id column, so local rows, tags and collections are not deleted while the route returns success. The next full sync removes them later

Issue titles that anyone can write on GitHub go into the prompt unguarded, and the summary is cached for all users. Any user can force a rewrite with refresh=true, and with their own key no quota applies
Raw user query is pasted into three prompts with no guard. Impact is limited to that user's own search
repoIds has no size cap and the route makes one sequential GitHub release call per starred repo, with no rate limit
Categorization cooldown is 7 days in code. README says 24 hours, AGENTS.md line 115 says 24h, and migration 010 is named daily limit
Discover cache TTL is 7 days in code and in migration 016. README says 30-day cache
tracesSampleRate fixed at 1.0 in all three Sentry configs
